renderedLegacyText:
Grand Canyon in 3 days is a great window — enough time to actually settle in and do it right, whether that's rim walks and sunsets or a serious below-the-rim hike.

Before I lock in the itinerary, I need two things that'll change the shape of this trip:

1. **Who's going?** Solo, couple, family with kids, bigger group — this affects trail picks and lodging.
2. **Fitness level?** The Grand Canyon's biggest trap is underestimating the hike back UP. If you want to go below the rim (Bright Angel, South Kaibab), I need to know if you're comfortable with sustained steep climbing in heat, or if you'd rather stick to rim trails and mule/shuttle viewpoints.

One quick note on logistics regardless of those answers: Grand Canyon doesn't currently have timed-entry requirements, which means no crowd control — South Rim parking lots (especially Mather Point, Yavapai, Grand Canyon Village) fill up by mid-morning in summer. Plan to be at your first viewpoint before 7am or expect to shuttle/park-and-walk.

I'd also default to basing you on the **South Rim** (Grand Canyon Village) since it's open year-round, has the most services, food, and lodging, and is the standard first-timer base — the North Rim is a solid alternative but adds a lot of driving (it's a 4-5hr drive around the canyon from the South Rim, not a quick hop). Let me know if you specifically want North Rim instead.

Once I know group size and fitness level, I can build the actual day-by-day — heat management in August matters a lot for anything below the rim (it regularly hits 100°F+ in the inner canyon).
